status: frozen before any model training beyond 1,000-step throughput benchmarks; GNS seed count (1, revisit after G0) set by the user 2026-09-29; gripper design approved by the user 2026-09-29
scope: model implementation, training configuration and exact G0 measurement. No gate, arm or threshold changes.

gripper.design: hand, left finger and right finger are ACTUATED objects: predicted like free objects, their nodes carrying a command feature (commanded target minus the current attachment-site position, 3 numbers; gripper closed state, 1 number) plus a node-type one-hot (static / dynamic / actuated) on every node
gripper.geometry: each part is the convex hull of the Panda's own collision geoms for that body (hand 102 vertices; each finger shell 45 vertices)
gripper.self_contacts: the three parts share one group, and FIGNet builds no face-face edges within a group. The 2026-09-29 design view found 594 such edges in a resting frame, more than all real contacts combined.
gripper.inputs_at_rollout: gripper poses for the first 3 input frames come from proprioception; afterwards they are the model's own predictions; the attachment site is computed from the predicted hand pose
gripper.arm_links: not modelled (34 of 1,794 new validation contacts)

port_changes: vendor/fignet_port.patch: dependency shims; ACTUATED kinematic type; optional per-node extra features; contact groups; the per-pair mesh copy in _cal_connectivity cached once per object (edges verified bit-identical on 9 graphs)

models.fignet: FIGNet* (mesh-mesh edges left out), latent 128, 10 message-passing rounds, 2-layer MLPs of width 128; 5,561,222 parameters
models.gns: object-level GNS, fully connected, latent 128, 10 rounds, 2-layer MLPs of width 128; 1,593,990 parameters. 'Matched size' = matched width, depth and MLP layout; parameter counts are reported, not equalised.

training.noise: Gaussian position noise sigma = 0.15 mm on moving nodes (the port's 0.03 mm scaled x5 for 5x longer steps); GNS also gets rotation noise sigma = 0.15 mm / 5 cm = 3 mrad
training.targets: clean next-step accelerations (the port's convention, used for both models)
training.loss: per-node MSE on normalized accelerations over all moving nodes (objects and gripper), the port's convention
training.batch: 8 random training episodes x 8 random samples (main or branch sequences), deterministic in (seed, batch index)
training.checkpoint_used: the final (400k) checkpoint of every run; no checkpoint selection on any held-out data
training.normalizers: frozen at evaluation (the port's normalizers otherwise keep accumulating when called)

G0_measurement.data: the 100 generic TEST trajectories (episodes 5100-5199), main sequences only; never used before this measurement
G0_measurement.windows: rollouts start at model steps t in {2, 22, 42, 62} of every trajectory (400 windows) from 3 true input frames, and run 20 model steps (2 s) with the recorded commands
G0_measurement.position_error: mean over windows, rollout steps 1-20 and free objects of the Euclidean error of predicted vs true object body positions, in metres
G0_measurement.interpenetration: for each window and rollout step, the maximum penetration depth among object/object and object/table pairs of the predicted configuration (coal, zero security margin); mean over windows and steps, in mm. The same quantity is reported on the true trajectories for reference.
G0_measurement.pass: median over the 3 FIGNet* seeds of position_error < the GNS seed-1 value, AND median FIGNet* interpenetration < 1 mm
G0_measurement.also_reported: per-seed values; rotation error; gripper (hand) position error; step-20 position error; ms per 64-probe x 38-step rollout batch; corpus throughput (7,310 episodes/h with 4 workers)
G0_measurement.fail: per protocol: switch to an in-repo FIGNet* implementation and repeat G0 once

compute: measured with 1,000-step benchmarks: FIGNet* 5.85 steps/s (14 data workers, GPU-bound), ~19 h per seed; GNS 29.3 steps/s, ~3.8 h
